scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO focuses on next-generation AI agent architectures powered by LLMs and large AI models, capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and action to achieve specified goals based on high-level instructions.

The project addresses robust planning, reasoning, and search mechanisms through a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with formally specified pre-conditions, post-conditions, and verification checkpoints, integrating Monte Carlo Tree Search and hierarchical task networks with LLM-driven heuristic evaluation.

The project develops an adaptive memory architecture integrating working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory — unified by a memory controller — to sustain coherent agent behaviour across extended interactions and long task horizons beyond any single LLM context window.

The project develops a cross-cutting External Tool and API Orchestration Layer providing a typed tool registry, formal tool selection and invocation policies, standardised API adapters for heterogeneous protocols (REST, GraphQL, HL7 FHIR, OPC-UA), post-invocation verification and grounding, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces — explicitly positioned to overcome limitations of large AI models in tasks requiring accuracy and reliability.

The project develops decentralised multi-agent coordination protocols enabling heterogeneous AI agents to decompose tasks, negotiate subtask assignments, establish shared commitment structures with provable convergence, and produce auditable delegation and decision traces.

Research activities span TRL 2 at project start — where core AI agent architectures, reasoning mechanisms, and coordination protocols are formulated and experimentally grounded — advancing to TRL 5 by project end through integrated validation in operational environments.

MAESTRO validates its research in the healthcare sector through a clinical decision support demonstrator co-designed with clinical partners, integrating HL7 FHIR connectors, diagnostic knowledge bases, and imaging analysis APIs, with performance assessed against quantitative KPIs including diagnostic accuracy, reasoning trace completeness, and tool invocation success rate.

MAESTRO validates its research in the advanced manufacturing sector through a process optimisation demonstrator validated in operational factory environments, integrating OPC-UA industrial connectors, digital twin APIs, and sensor data streams, with progress monitored via KPIs including defect rate reduction, energy savings, and multi-agent coordination latency.

MAESTRO includes a logistics and supply chain operations cross-sector transfer demonstrator that confirms architecture portability beyond the call's three specifically identified Apply AI sectors (healthcare, advanced manufacturing, in-vehicle autonomous driving), exercising planning, multi-agent coordination, and tool orchestration capabilities with logistics tracking, customs clearance, and carrier scheduling APIs.

MAESTRO does not include in-vehicle autonomous driving as a full sector demonstrator because the consortium does not include automotive sector partners; instead, it includes a targeted architectural mapping analysis in WP8 assessing the MAESTRO architecture's transferability to autonomous driving settings.
MAESTRO allocates dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with the European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics (ADRA) and with the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).

All research outputs — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities and disseminated via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).
MAESTRO will link to the resources offered by AI Factories and Data Labs for compute-intensive training and evaluation.
MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured 6-month integration checkpoints for progress monitoring.
MAESTRO contributes to the Apply AI Strategy by advancing foundational AI agent capabilities enabling trustworthy AI deployment in key European economic sectors.
Project duration is stated as 48 months.
scope_findings.flag_reason: The claimed 48-month duration equals the maximum boundary recorded in CC-14. However, CC-14 carries status 'Assumed' with an explicit assumption_note stating that 48 months is not confirmed in the Tier 2B topic text and is pending verification against Tier 1 General Annex B. No entry in scope_requirements.json (SR-01 through SR-11) addresses project duration; the constraint boundary derives exclusively from CC-14. Because the constraint boundary has not been confirmed from a Tier 1 source, the claim cannot be definitively assessed as within scope. If the verified maximum duration differs from 48 months, the claimed duration may require revision before Phase 8 content is finalised.

scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO's open-source framework and standardised agent interaction protocols will lower barriers for European SMEs and startups to build on next-generation AI agent technology, strengthening the European AI ecosystem.
